# Code Review Standards

> These standards apply to all code — whether written by a developer,
> generated by AI, or suggested by Copilot. AI-generated code is not
> exempt from review requirements.

## The Definition of Done

Code is not complete when it runs. Code is complete when it:

- [ ] Implements the feature or fix correctly
- [ ] Has clear variable and function names (no cryptic abbreviations)
- [ ] Has test coverage or validation for core logic
- [ ] Passes `npm run build` with no errors
- [ ] Has no hardcoded magic numbers or strings
- [ ] Has inline comments for non-obvious logic
- [ ] Has no unnecessary console.log or debugging code

## What Copilot Should Flag in Any Code Review

### 🔴 Reject — Must Fix Before Merge

These are non-negotiable. Do not approve code with any of these:

- Hardcoded magic numbers without named constants
- console.log, console.error, or console.warn left in production code
- Unhandled async operations (missing try/catch)
- localStorage access without error handling
- JSON.parse without try/catch
- Missing validation before saving data
- Secrets or API keys in source code
- `test.only` or `test.skip` without explanation
- Breaking changes without updating CHANGELOG

### 🟡 Flag — Should Fix, Can Discuss

These are strong preferences. Flag them and discuss before merging:

- Missing error handling on user interactions
- No validation on form inputs
- Function longer than ~150 lines — consider splitting
- Missing comments on complex game logic
- Using `var` instead of `const`/`let`
- Promise chains instead of async/await
- No JSDoc comments on exported functions

### 🟢 Approve — Good Patterns to Reinforce

Acknowledge and reinforce these when you see them:

- Clear error messages for users
- Proper localStorage error handling
- Async/await with try/catch
- Descriptive variable names
- Useful comments on business logic
- Graceful fallbacks for missing data

## AI-Generated Code Review Checklist

Copilot and other AI tools can generate plausible-looking but
subtly incorrect code. Apply extra scrutiny to AI-generated code:

- [ ] No unhandled async operations
- [ ] localStorage access is wrapped in try/catch
- [ ] JSON.parse is wrapped in try/catch
- [ ] No obvious infinite loops or performance issues
- [ ] No breaking changes to existing functions
- [ ] No secrets or credentials
- [ ] No unnecessary console.log calls
- [ ] Variable names are clear and descriptive

## Patterns That Signal a Deeper Problem

If you see these, raise them — they usually mean a larger issue
needs addressing, not just a line fix:

- Repeated error handling code in many places
  → signals a missing shared error utility
- Multiple places checking the same game rules
  → signals rules should be centralized
- Growing list of function parameters
  → signals the function is doing too much
- Similar game logic duplicated across views
  → signals a missing shared utility or function

## Commit Message Format

Follow Keep a Changelog conventions. Every commit message must
start with one of these keywords:

| Keyword     | Use for                                            |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `ADD`       | New features                                       |
| `UPDATE`    | Changes to existing functionality                  |
| `DEPRECATE` | Features marked for upcoming removal               |
| `REMOVE`    | Features that have been deleted                    |
| `FIX`       | Bug fixes                                          |
| `SECURITY`  | Security vulnerability fixes                       |
| `AUDIT`     | Code cleanup; careful removal of unnecessary files |

```bash
# ✅ correct
ADD: character sheet export to JSON
FIX: character builder crash when no armor equipped
AUDIT: remove unused CSS from styles.css

# ❌ avoid
fixed bug
updated stuff
WIP
```
